Comments (English): [ Bosch 800 Series Dishwasher ] || ---------------- || My new Bosch dishwasher does a good job of cleaning dishes, as my old one did. If I wanted to add a forgotten dish before it started, I could do that, just being sure to fully close the door again. With the new model, there is no delayed start feature! I need to use an app on my phone, which works only some of the time. It means that if I am away, my family members have no delayed start option. I t is not possible to add a dish after setting up the delay on the app without causing the program to fail. Then I have to reset the machine and run it manually in the morning. Why on earth would Bosch remove a useful feature and replace it with an inconvenient app?

Sentence (English): I ordered this just in time for the kids' school vacation.
Comments (English): I ordered this just in time for the kids' school vacation. When vacation starts, the dishwashing hell begins. Since I do a lot of work, my finger joints, wrists, elbows, and shoulders all ache, so I was determined to buy a dishwasher this time. A Samsung technician came and kindly installed it for me. The usage is much more intuitive than I expected. After the first wash, there was a fishy smell coming from the cups. When I smelled them closely, I realized the new plastic smell had lingered as a fishy odor after the hot air drying. The smell disappeared after using it a few times. I am extremely satisfied because I can put in the evening dishes and do other things during that time. I hope to continue using it without any breakdowns.
Comments (Original): 아이들 방학 에 맞춰서 주문했어요. 방학이 되면 설거지 지옥이 시작 돼요. 지안 일을 많이 하다 보니 손가락 관절과 손목 팔꿈치 어깨 안 아픈 곳이 없어서 이번에 꼭 식기세척기를 구매 하고자 마음 먹었어요. 삼성 기사님 께서 오셔서 친절하게 설치 해 주셨어요.사용법은 생각보다 굉장히 직관적이에요. 처음 설거지 후에 비린냄새가 나서 컵에서 비린내가 나더라구요. 자세히 맡아 보니 플라스틱 새 냄새가 열풍 건조 후에 비린 냄새로 남더라구요.몇 번 사용후 냄새는 없어졌습니다저녁 설거지 넣어놓고 그 시간에 다른 일을 할 수 있어서 너무 너무 만족합니다. 앞으로 고장 없이 쭉 잘 사용 했으면 좋겠어요.

Sentence (English): Title: I Escaped the Dishwashing Swamp!
Comments (English): Title: I Escaped the Dishwashing Swamp! Highly Recommended for 2-3 Person Households (Includes Chopstick Tip). I purchased this Samsung Bespoke Countertop 6-Place Dishwasher after being stressed out by the daily pile of dishes. The technician who came for installation was so kind, explained everything thoroughly, and installed everything neatly, so I felt good right from the start. After using it, I feel like I’ve completely escaped the dishwashing swamp—I should have bought this sooner! It is the perfect size for collecting and running a day's worth of dishes for a 2-3 person household. If you just roughly rinse off large food residue and put everything in, it cleans up better than expected, leaving everything squeaky clean. The clean white design really brings the kitchen interior to life. The only downside is that chopsticks keep slipping through the holes in the cutlery holder and sometimes get caught on the wings. You can perfectly solve this by inserting the cutlery with the thicker end facing down or by adding a small cutlery rack like the one from Daiso! I highly recommend this to households of 2 to 3 people who want to escape the stress of dishwashing and improve their quality of life!

Sentence (English): This is a truly honest review after using the LG dishwasher for about a year.
Comments (English): This is a truly honest review after using the LG dishwasher for about a year. Before I bought it, I was the most opposed to it, saying, "Scrubbing by hand is cleaner; why buy a dishwasher for just a few dishes?" But now that I have it in my home, I painfully understand why everyone calls the dryer, robot vacuum, and dishwasher the "three major home appliances." Here are some moments I was truly satisfied with: The satisfaction of seeing grease come off cleanly is incredible. Even if I put in a frying pan covered in grease after grilling pork belly or bowls that held beef bone broth, they come out squeaky clean. It feels much cleaner and more hygienic to use high-temperature steam to scrub them thoroughly rather than scrubbing with detergent in cold or lukewarm water. You just run it at night and go to sleep (the door opens automatically). Once the wash is finished, the door slides open slightly, letting the steam escape. There is no risk of odors getting trapped, and it is incredibly convenient to have everything dry and fluffy by the next morning after just running it overnight. I get 'free time' in the evenings. Before, I used to sigh at the mountain of dishes piled up after cooking and eating, but now I just rinse the large food scraps with water, toss them into the dishwasher, and that's it. I can relax for at least 30 minutes after dinner. Realistic downsides you must know before buying: It isn't completely 'labor-free' (pre-washing is essential). It cannot perfectly remove hard-dried rice grains or burnt bottoms of pots. You still need to put in the effort to soak them in water beforehand or give them a quick pre-rinse. You need 'dish Tetris' know-how. Since many Korean dishes are deep rice and soup bowls, you need a bit of skill (?) to stack them upright so the water flow aligns well. You will have to use your head a bit for the first few days to fit the dishes in. Definitely go for the large capacity. If you buy a 6-place setting or a smaller one just because you are a 1-2 person household, you won't even be able to fit pots or pans, and you will end up washing them by hand. If space allows, I strongly recommend purchasing a 12-place setting or larger. In short: For those who struggle with family members over dishwashing turns or simply don't want to lift a finger after work, this is an appliance that is definitely worth the money and will dramatically improve your quality of life!

Before I bought it, I was the most opposed to it, saying, "Scrubbing by hand is cleaner; why buy a dishwasher for just a few dishes?" But now that I have it in my home, I painfully understand why everyone calls the dryer, robot vacuum, and dishwasher the "three major home appliances." Here are some moments I was truly satisfied with: The satisfaction of seeing grease come off cleanly is incredible. Even if I put in a frying pan covered in grease after grilling pork belly or bowls that held beef bone broth, they come out squeaky clean. It feels much cleaner and more hygienic to use high-temperature steam to scrub them thoroughly rather than scrubbing with detergent in cold or lukewarm water. You just run it at night and go to sleep (the door opens automatically). Once the wash is finished, the door slides open slightly, letting the steam escape. There is no risk of odors getting trapped, and it is incredibly convenient to have everything dry and fluffy by the next morning after just running it overnight. I get 'free time' in the evenings. Before, I used to sigh at the mountain of dishes piled up after cooking and eating, but now I just rinse the large food scraps with water, toss them into the dishwasher, and that's it. I can relax for at least 30 minutes after dinner. Realistic downsides you must know before buying: It isn't completely 'labor-free' (pre-washing is essential). It cannot perfectly remove hard-dried rice grains or burnt bottoms of pots. You still need to put in the effort to soak them in water beforehand or give them a quick pre-rinse. You need 'dish Tetris' know-how. Since many Korean dishes are deep rice and soup bowls, you need a bit of skill (?) to stack them upright so the water flow aligns well. You will have to use your head a bit for the first few days to fit the dishes in. Definitely go for the large capacity. If you buy a 6-place setting or a smaller one just because you are a 1-2 person household, you won't even be able to fit pots or pans, and you will end up washing them by hand. If space allows, I strongly recommend purchasing a 12-place setting or larger. In short: For those who struggle with family members over dishwashing turns or simply don't want to lift a finger after work, this is an appliance that is definitely worth the money and will dramatically improve your quality of life!

Sentence (English): Even if I put in a frying pan covered in grease after grilling pork belly or bowls that held beef bone broth, they come out squeaky clean.
Comments (English): This is a truly honest review after using the LG dishwasher for about a year. Before I bought it, I was the most opposed to it, saying, "Scrubbing by hand is cleaner; why buy a dishwasher for just a few dishes?" But now that I have it in my home, I painfully understand why everyone calls the dryer, robot vacuum, and dishwasher the "three major home appliances." Here are some moments I was truly satisfied with: The satisfaction of seeing grease come off cleanly is incredible. Even if I put in a frying pan covered in grease after grilling pork belly or bowls that held beef bone broth, they come out squeaky clean. It feels much cleaner and more hygienic to use high-temperature steam to scrub them thoroughly rather than scrubbing with detergent in cold or lukewarm water. You just run it at night and go to sleep (the door opens automatically). Once the wash is finished, the door slides open slightly, letting the steam escape. There is no risk of odors getting trapped, and it is incredibly convenient to have everything dry and fluffy by the next morning after just running it overnight. I get 'free time' in the evenings. Before, I used to sigh at the mountain of dishes piled up after cooking and eating, but now I just rinse the large food scraps with water, toss them into the dishwasher, and that's it. I can relax for at least 30 minutes after dinner. Realistic downsides you must know before buying: It isn't completely 'labor-free' (pre-washing is essential). It cannot perfectly remove hard-dried rice grains or burnt bottoms of pots. You still need to put in the effort to soak them in water beforehand or give them a quick pre-rinse. You need 'dish Tetris' know-how. Since many Korean dishes are deep rice and soup bowls, you need a bit of skill (?) to stack them upright so the water flow aligns well. You will have to use your head a bit for the first few days to fit the dishes in. Definitely go for the large capacity. If you buy a 6-place setting or a smaller one just because you are a 1-2 person household, you won't even be able to fit pots or pans, and you will end up washing them by hand. If space allows, I strongly recommend purchasing a 12-place setting or larger. In short: For those who struggle with family members over dishwashing turns or simply don't want to lift a finger after work, this is an appliance that is definitely worth the money and will dramatically improve your quality of life!

Sentence (English): Once the wash is finished, the door slides open slightly, letting the steam escape.
Comments (English): This is a truly honest review after using the LG dishwasher for about a year. Before I bought it, I was the most opposed to it, saying, "Scrubbing by hand is cleaner; why buy a dishwasher for just a few dishes?" But now that I have it in my home, I painfully understand why everyone calls the dryer, robot vacuum, and dishwasher the "three major home appliances." Here are some moments I was truly satisfied with: The satisfaction of seeing grease come off cleanly is incredible. Even if I put in a frying pan covered in grease after grilling pork belly or bowls that held beef bone broth, they come out squeaky clean. It feels much cleaner and more hygienic to use high-temperature steam to scrub them thoroughly rather than scrubbing with detergent in cold or lukewarm water. You just run it at night and go to sleep (the door opens automatically). Once the wash is finished, the door slides open slightly, letting the steam escape. There is no risk of odors getting trapped, and it is incredibly convenient to have everything dry and fluffy by the next morning after just running it overnight. I get 'free time' in the evenings. Before, I used to sigh at the mountain of dishes piled up after cooking and eating, but now I just rinse the large food scraps with water, toss them into the dishwasher, and that's it. I can relax for at least 30 minutes after dinner. Realistic downsides you must know before buying: It isn't completely 'labor-free' (pre-washing is essential). It cannot perfectly remove hard-dried rice grains or burnt bottoms of pots. You still need to put in the effort to soak them in water beforehand or give them a quick pre-rinse. You need 'dish Tetris' know-how. Since many Korean dishes are deep rice and soup bowls, you need a bit of skill (?) to stack them upright so the water flow aligns well. You will have to use your head a bit for the first few days to fit the dishes in. Definitely go for the large capacity. If you buy a 6-place setting or a smaller one just because you are a 1-2 person household, you won't even be able to fit pots or pans, and you will end up washing them by hand. If space allows, I strongly recommend purchasing a 12-place setting or larger. In short: For those who struggle with family members over dishwashing turns or simply don't want to lift a finger after work, this is an appliance that is definitely worth the money and will dramatically improve your quality of life!

Sentence (English): Before, I used to sigh at the mountain of dishes piled up after cooking and eating, but now I just rinse the large food scraps with water, toss them into the dishwasher, and that's it.
Comments (English): This is a truly honest review after using the LG dishwasher for about a year. Before I bought it, I was the most opposed to it, saying, "Scrubbing by hand is cleaner; why buy a dishwasher for just a few dishes?" But now that I have it in my home, I painfully understand why everyone calls the dryer, robot vacuum, and dishwasher the "three major home appliances." Here are some moments I was truly satisfied with: The satisfaction of seeing grease come off cleanly is incredible. Even if I put in a frying pan covered in grease after grilling pork belly or bowls that held beef bone broth, they come out squeaky clean. It feels much cleaner and more hygienic to use high-temperature steam to scrub them thoroughly rather than scrubbing with detergent in cold or lukewarm water. You just run it at night and go to sleep (the door opens automatically). Once the wash is finished, the door slides open slightly, letting the steam escape. There is no risk of odors getting trapped, and it is incredibly convenient to have everything dry and fluffy by the next morning after just running it overnight. I get 'free time' in the evenings. Before, I used to sigh at the mountain of dishes piled up after cooking and eating, but now I just rinse the large food scraps with water, toss them into the dishwasher, and that's it. I can relax for at least 30 minutes after dinner. Realistic downsides you must know before buying: It isn't completely 'labor-free' (pre-washing is essential). It cannot perfectly remove hard-dried rice grains or burnt bottoms of pots. You still need to put in the effort to soak them in water beforehand or give them a quick pre-rinse. You need 'dish Tetris' know-how. Since many Korean dishes are deep rice and soup bowls, you need a bit of skill (?) to stack them upright so the water flow aligns well. You will have to use your head a bit for the first few days to fit the dishes in. Definitely go for the large capacity. If you buy a 6-place setting or a smaller one just because you are a 1-2 person household, you won't even be able to fit pots or pans, and you will end up washing them by hand. If space allows, I strongly recommend purchasing a 12-place setting or larger. In short: For those who struggle with family members over dishwashing turns or simply don't want to lift a finger after work, this is an appliance that is definitely worth the money and will dramatically improve your quality of life!

Sentence (English): Realistic downsides you must know before buying: It isn't completely 'labor-free' (pre-washing is essential).
Comments (English): This is a truly honest review after using the LG dishwasher for about a year. Before I bought it, I was the most opposed to it, saying, "Scrubbing by hand is cleaner; why buy a dishwasher for just a few dishes?" But now that I have it in my home, I painfully understand why everyone calls the dryer, robot vacuum, and dishwasher the "three major home appliances." Here are some moments I was truly satisfied with: The satisfaction of seeing grease come off cleanly is incredible. Even if I put in a frying pan covered in grease after grilling pork belly or bowls that held beef bone broth, they come out squeaky clean. It feels much cleaner and more hygienic to use high-temperature steam to scrub them thoroughly rather than scrubbing with detergent in cold or lukewarm water. You just run it at night and go to sleep (the door opens automatically). Once the wash is finished, the door slides open slightly, letting the steam escape. There is no risk of odors getting trapped, and it is incredibly convenient to have everything dry and fluffy by the next morning after just running it overnight. I get 'free time' in the evenings. Before, I used to sigh at the mountain of dishes piled up after cooking and eating, but now I just rinse the large food scraps with water, toss them into the dishwasher, and that's it. I can relax for at least 30 minutes after dinner. Realistic downsides you must know before buying: It isn't completely 'labor-free' (pre-washing is essential). It cannot perfectly remove hard-dried rice grains or burnt bottoms of pots. You still need to put in the effort to soak them in water beforehand or give them a quick pre-rinse. You need 'dish Tetris' know-how. Since many Korean dishes are deep rice and soup bowls, you need a bit of skill (?) to stack them upright so the water flow aligns well. You will have to use your head a bit for the first few days to fit the dishes in. Definitely go for the large capacity. If you buy a 6-place setting or a smaller one just because you are a 1-2 person household, you won't even be able to fit pots or pans, and you will end up washing them by hand. If space allows, I strongly recommend purchasing a 12-place setting or larger. In short: For those who struggle with family members over dishwashing turns or simply don't want to lift a finger after work, this is an appliance that is definitely worth the money and will dramatically improve your quality of life!

Sentence (English): You need 'dish Tetris' know-how.
Comments (English): This is a truly honest review after using the LG dishwasher for about a year. Before I bought it, I was the most opposed to it, saying, "Scrubbing by hand is cleaner; why buy a dishwasher for just a few dishes?" But now that I have it in my home, I painfully understand why everyone calls the dryer, robot vacuum, and dishwasher the "three major home appliances." Here are some moments I was truly satisfied with: The satisfaction of seeing grease come off cleanly is incredible. Even if I put in a frying pan covered in grease after grilling pork belly or bowls that held beef bone broth, they come out squeaky clean. It feels much cleaner and more hygienic to use high-temperature steam to scrub them thoroughly rather than scrubbing with detergent in cold or lukewarm water. You just run it at night and go to sleep (the door opens automatically). Once the wash is finished, the door slides open slightly, letting the steam escape. There is no risk of odors getting trapped, and it is incredibly convenient to have everything dry and fluffy by the next morning after just running it overnight. I get 'free time' in the evenings. Before, I used to sigh at the mountain of dishes piled up after cooking and eating, but now I just rinse the large food scraps with water, toss them into the dishwasher, and that's it. I can relax for at least 30 minutes after dinner. Realistic downsides you must know before buying: It isn't completely 'labor-free' (pre-washing is essential). It cannot perfectly remove hard-dried rice grains or burnt bottoms of pots. You still need to put in the effort to soak them in water beforehand or give them a quick pre-rinse. You need 'dish Tetris' know-how. Since many Korean dishes are deep rice and soup bowls, you need a bit of skill (?) to stack them upright so the water flow aligns well. You will have to use your head a bit for the first few days to fit the dishes in. Definitely go for the large capacity. If you buy a 6-place setting or a smaller one just because you are a 1-2 person household, you won't even be able to fit pots or pans, and you will end up washing them by hand. If space allows, I strongly recommend purchasing a 12-place setting or larger. In short: For those who struggle with family members over dishwashing turns or simply don't want to lift a finger after work, this is an appliance that is definitely worth the money and will dramatically improve your quality of life!

Comments (English): This is a truly honest review after using the LG dishwasher for about a year. Before I bought it, I was the most opposed to it, saying, "Scrubbing by hand is cleaner; why buy a dishwasher for just a few dishes?" But now that I have it in my home, I painfully understand why everyone calls the dryer, robot vacuum, and dishwasher the "three major home appliances." Here are some moments I was truly satisfied with: The satisfaction of seeing grease come off cleanly is incredible. Even if I put in a frying pan covered in grease after grilling pork belly or bowls that held beef bone broth, they come out squeaky clean. It feels much cleaner and more hygienic to use high-temperature steam to scrub them thoroughly rather than scrubbing with detergent in cold or lukewarm water. You just run it at night and go to sleep (the door opens automatically). Once the wash is finished, the door slides open slightly, letting the steam escape. There is no risk of odors getting trapped, and it is incredibly convenient to have everything dry and fluffy by the next morning after just running it overnight. I get 'free time' in the evenings. Before, I used to sigh at the mountain of dishes piled up after cooking and eating, but now I just rinse the large food scraps with water, toss them into the dishwasher, and that's it. I can relax for at least 30 minutes after dinner. Realistic downsides you must know before buying: It isn't completely 'labor-free' (pre-washing is essential). It cannot perfectly remove hard-dried rice grains or burnt bottoms of pots. You still need to put in the effort to soak them in water beforehand or give them a quick pre-rinse. You need 'dish Tetris' know-how. Since many Korean dishes are deep rice and soup bowls, you need a bit of skill (?) to stack them upright so the water flow aligns well. You will have to use your head a bit for the first few days to fit the dishes in. Definitely go for the large capacity. If you buy a 6-place setting or a smaller one just because you are a 1-2 person household, you won't even be able to fit pots or pans, and you will end up washing them by hand. If space allows, I strongly recommend purchasing a 12-place setting or larger. In short: For those who struggle with family members over dishwashing turns or simply don't want to lift a finger after work, this is an appliance that is definitely worth the money and will dramatically improve your quality of life!

Sentence (English): If you buy a 6-place setting or a smaller one just because you are a 1-2 person household, you won't even be able to fit pots or pans, and you will end up washing them by hand.
Comments (English): This is a truly honest review after using the LG dishwasher for about a year. Before I bought it, I was the most opposed to it, saying, "Scrubbing by hand is cleaner; why buy a dishwasher for just a few dishes?" But now that I have it in my home, I painfully understand why everyone calls the dryer, robot vacuum, and dishwasher the "three major home appliances." Here are some moments I was truly satisfied with: The satisfaction of seeing grease come off cleanly is incredible. Even if I put in a frying pan covered in grease after grilling pork belly or bowls that held beef bone broth, they come out squeaky clean. It feels much cleaner and more hygienic to use high-temperature steam to scrub them thoroughly rather than scrubbing with detergent in cold or lukewarm water. You just run it at night and go to sleep (the door opens automatically). Once the wash is finished, the door slides open slightly, letting the steam escape. There is no risk of odors getting trapped, and it is incredibly convenient to have everything dry and fluffy by the next morning after just running it overnight. I get 'free time' in the evenings. Before, I used to sigh at the mountain of dishes piled up after cooking and eating, but now I just rinse the large food scraps with water, toss them into the dishwasher, and that's it. I can relax for at least 30 minutes after dinner. Realistic downsides you must know before buying: It isn't completely 'labor-free' (pre-washing is essential). It cannot perfectly remove hard-dried rice grains or burnt bottoms of pots. You still need to put in the effort to soak them in water beforehand or give them a quick pre-rinse. You need 'dish Tetris' know-how. Since many Korean dishes are deep rice and soup bowls, you need a bit of skill (?) to stack them upright so the water flow aligns well. You will have to use your head a bit for the first few days to fit the dishes in. Definitely go for the large capacity. If you buy a 6-place setting or a smaller one just because you are a 1-2 person household, you won't even be able to fit pots or pans, and you will end up washing them by hand. If space allows, I strongly recommend purchasing a 12-place setting or larger. In short: For those who struggle with family members over dishwashing turns or simply don't want to lift a finger after work, this is an appliance that is definitely worth the money and will dramatically improve your quality of life!

Sentence (English): After a number of disappointments with LG's product line (like the motor sounding like a jet engine after merely 5 years), I decided to take a chance on this KitchenAid.
Comments (English): [ So glad I got this brand! ] || ---------------- || After a number of disappointments with LG's product line (like the motor sounding like a jet engine after merely 5 years), I decided to take a chance on this KitchenAid. I can't believe how quiet it is, and I don't mean in comparison to a jet engine. I had a third rack in the old LG, but it was nothing like this. It had like a two inch clearance for basically flat utensils only. In the KitchenAid, you can practically fit all your glasses, mugs, and small bowls up top and it gets everything clean as a whistle. This design is absolutely genius. Also, I recently placed a metal coffee pod that was really ugly up here in the third rack — I can't believe what it looks like now. Shiny stainless steel - amazing. And, the middle rack provides so much room for larger bowls and small plates (like for your pets), I barely even use the lower rack. In fact, you can set the washer to just wash the upper racks if you want to. Utensil basket is well designed and leaves everything sparkly. Also, I love the door open feature where some time after the drying cycle has ended, the door automatically pops open a few inches to get rid of condensation. Again, another brilliant function. I thought I had a ghost until I figured out what was happening. I'd go down to my kitchen in the morning and see the door popped open! Eerie! LOL! Anyway, it washes and dries so well, I've only had to use the Express wash and Pro-dry functions, which are the bare minimums. The exterior stainless steel really cleans up well, and the handle provides a place for a kitchen towel, if need be. Lastly, day-to-day maintenance so far has been a breeze. No more nasty filter to clean out. This one just has a large debris cup that you just have to eyeball to make sure nothing fell down to the bottom. I will say I had gotten used to LG's hidden heating element and how that always eased my mind that nothing could fall on it and burn, but then again, it never dried the dishes well at all. In the KitchenAid, there is a narrow exposed element but I'm just careful to make sure all the dishes are well secured above. It dries like a dream.

I can't believe how quiet it is, and I don't mean in comparison to a jet engine. I had a third rack in the old LG, but it was nothing like this. It had like a two inch clearance for basically flat utensils only. In the KitchenAid, you can practically fit all your glasses, mugs, and small bowls up top and it gets everything clean as a whistle. This design is absolutely genius. Also, I recently placed a metal coffee pod that was really ugly up here in the third rack — I can't believe what it looks like now. Shiny stainless steel - amazing. And, the middle rack provides so much room for larger bowls and small plates (like for your pets), I barely even use the lower rack. In fact, you can set the washer to just wash the upper racks if you want to. Utensil basket is well designed and leaves everything sparkly. Also, I love the door open feature where some time after the drying cycle has ended, the door automatically pops open a few inches to get rid of condensation. Again, another brilliant function. I thought I had a ghost until I figured out what was happening. I'd go down to my kitchen in the morning and see the door popped open! Eerie! LOL! Anyway, it washes and dries so well, I've only had to use the Express wash and Pro-dry functions, which are the bare minimums. The exterior stainless steel really cleans up well, and the handle provides a place for a kitchen towel, if need be. Lastly, day-to-day maintenance so far has been a breeze. No more nasty filter to clean out. This one just has a large debris cup that you just have to eyeball to make sure nothing fell down to the bottom. I will say I had gotten used to LG's hidden heating element and how that always eased my mind that nothing could fall on it and burn, but then again, it never dried the dishes well at all. In the KitchenAid, there is a narrow exposed element but I'm just careful to make sure all the dishes are well secured above. It dries like a dream.

Sentence (English): This dishwasher feels like a much better use of space than the traditional dishwasher design.
Comments (English): [ The future of dishwashers ] || ---------------- || This dishwasher feels like a much better use of space than the traditional dishwasher design. I love to not have to bend over as far for the main load of the dishwasher. It is wonderful to have the flexibility to use the lower drawer as a completely separate dishwasher or to simply store other items for occasional use such as strainers and other items. This should really be the new standard for dishwasher configuration. My only criticism is that water tends to pool around the inner lip edge of the top drawer when you pull it out. It stays in the dishwasher of course but i always feel compelled to wipe it off before I start unloading. Maybe it could be slightly slanted downwards to allow for natural draining.

Sentence (English): This is a truly honest review after using the LG dishwasher for about a year.
Comments (English): This is a truly honest review after using the LG dishwasher for about a year. Before I bought it, I was the most opposed to it, saying, "Scrubbing by hand is cleaner; why buy a dishwasher for just a few dishes?" But now that I have it in my home, I painfully understand why everyone calls the dryer, robot vacuum, and dishwasher the "three major home appliances." Here are some moments I was truly satisfied with: The satisfaction of seeing grease come off cleanly is incredible. Even if I put in a frying pan smothered in grease after grilling pork belly or bowls that held beef bone broth, they come out squeaky clean. It feels much cleaner and more hygienic to use high-temperature steam to scrub them thoroughly rather than scrubbing with detergent in cold or lukewarm water. You just run it at night and go to sleep (the door opens automatically). Once the wash is finished, the door slides open slightly, letting the steam escape. There is no risk of odors getting trapped, and it is incredibly convenient to have everything dry and fluffy by the next morning after just running it overnight. It gives me "free time" in the evenings. I used to sigh at the mountain of dishes piled up after cooking and eating, but now I just rinse the large food scraps with water, toss them into the dishwasher, and that's it. I can relax for at least 30 minutes after dinner. Here are some realistic downsides you must know before buying: It isn't completely "labor-free" (pre-washing is essential). It cannot perfectly remove hardened dried-on rice grains or burnt bottoms of pots. You still need to put in the effort to soak them in water beforehand or give them a quick pre-rinse. You also need some "dish Tetris" know-how. Since many Korean dishes are deep rice and soup bowls, you need a bit of skill (?) to stack them upright so the water flow is aligned properly. You will have to use your head a bit for the first few days trying to fit the dishes in. Definitely go for the large capacity. If you buy a 6-person or small model just because you are a 1-2 person household, you won't even be able to fit pots or pans, and you will end up washing them by hand. If space allows, I strongly recommend buying a 12-person capacity or larger. One-line summary: For those who struggle with family members over dishwashing turns or simply don't want to lift a finger after work, this is a sure-fire appliance that dramatically improves your quality of life and is definitely worth the money!
Comments (Original): LG 식기세척기 1년 정도 써보고 남기는 진짜 솔직한 후기예요.처음 사기 전에는 '손으로 직접 빡빡 문질러 닦는 게 깨끗하지, 그릇 몇 개 된다고 식세기를 사?' 하고 제일 반대했었거든요. 근데 막상 집에 들여놓고 보니까 왜 다들 '건조기, 로봇청소기, 식기세척기는 3대 가전 이모님'이라고 부르는지 뼈저리게 느끼고 있습니다. 쓰면서 진짜 만족했던 순간들 기름때 깔끔하게 빠질 때 쾌감이 대단해요삼겹살 구워 먹고 기름 범벅된 프라이팬이나 사골 국물 담았던 그릇을 넣어도 뽀득뽀득하게 닦여서 나와요. 사람이 찬물/미온수로 세제 문지르는 것보다 고온 스팀으로 확 지져주는 게 훨씬 깔끔하고 위생적인 느낌입니다. 밤에 돌려두고 그냥 자면 끝이에요 (자동 문열림)세척이 끝나면 문이 스르륵 살짝 열리면서 수증기가 쫙 빠집니다. 냄새 갇힐 일도 없고, 밤에 돌려놓고 그냥 자면 다음 날 아침에 보송보송하게 말라 있어서 진짜 편해요. 저녁에 '자유 시간'이 생겨요요리하고 밥 먹고 나면 산더미처럼 쌓인 설거지거리 보면서 한숨부터 나왔는데, 지금은 물로 큼직한 음식물만 쓱 헹궈서 식세기에 던져 넣으면 끝입니다. 저녁 먹고 최소 30분은 느긋하게 쉴 수 있어요. 사기 전에 꼭 알아둬야 할 현실적인 단점 완벽한 '무노동'은 아니에요 (애벌 세척 필수)딱딱하게 말라붙은 밥풀이나 까맣게 탄 냄비 밑바닥까지 완벽하게 지워주진 못해요. 물에 미리 불려두거나 애벌로 쓱 한번 헹궈서 넣어주는 수고는 필요합니다. '그릇 테트리스' 노하우가 필요해요우리나라 그릇은 오목한 밥그릇, 국그릇이 많다 보니 물살이 잘 맞도록 세워 넣는 기술(?)이 좀 필요합니다. 처음 며칠은 그릇 끼워 넣느라 머리 좀 쓰셔야 해요. 용량은 무조건 큰 걸로 가세요1~2인 가구라고 6인용이나 작은 거 사시면 냄비나 프라이팬은 넣지도 못하고 결국 손설거지하게 됩니다. 자리만 된다면 무조건 12인용 이상으로 사시는 걸 강력 추천합니다. 한 줄 요약설거지 때문에 가족끼리 순번 정하며 눈치 싸움하거나, 퇴근 후 손가락 하나 꼼짝하기 싫은 분들에겐 삶의 질을 수직 상승시켜 주는 돈값 확실한 가전입니다!

Sentence (English): Here are some moments I was truly satisfied with: The satisfaction of seeing grease come off cleanly is incredible.
Comments (English): This is a truly honest review after using the LG dishwasher for about a year. Before I bought it, I was the most opposed to it, saying, "Scrubbing by hand is cleaner; why buy a dishwasher for just a few dishes?" But now that I have it in my home, I painfully understand why everyone calls the dryer, robot vacuum, and dishwasher the "three major home appliances." Here are some moments I was truly satisfied with: The satisfaction of seeing grease come off cleanly is incredible. Even if I put in a frying pan smothered in grease after grilling pork belly or bowls that held beef bone broth, they come out squeaky clean. It feels much cleaner and more hygienic to use high-temperature steam to scrub them thoroughly rather than scrubbing with detergent in cold or lukewarm water. You just run it at night and go to sleep (the door opens automatically). Once the wash is finished, the door slides open slightly, letting the steam escape. There is no risk of odors getting trapped, and it is incredibly convenient to have everything dry and fluffy by the next morning after just running it overnight. It gives me "free time" in the evenings. I used to sigh at the mountain of dishes piled up after cooking and eating, but now I just rinse the large food scraps with water, toss them into the dishwasher, and that's it. I can relax for at least 30 minutes after dinner. Here are some realistic downsides you must know before buying: It isn't completely "labor-free" (pre-washing is essential). It cannot perfectly remove hardened dried-on rice grains or burnt bottoms of pots. You still need to put in the effort to soak them in water beforehand or give them a quick pre-rinse. You also need some "dish Tetris" know-how. Since many Korean dishes are deep rice and soup bowls, you need a bit of skill (?) to stack them upright so the water flow is aligned properly. You will have to use your head a bit for the first few days trying to fit the dishes in. Definitely go for the large capacity. If you buy a 6-person or small model just because you are a 1-2 person household, you won't even be able to fit pots or pans, and you will end up washing them by hand. If space allows, I strongly recommend buying a 12-person capacity or larger. One-line summary: For those who struggle with family members over dishwashing turns or simply don't want to lift a finger after work, this is a sure-fire appliance that dramatically improves your quality of life and is definitely worth the money!

Sentence (English): It feels much cleaner and more hygienic to use high-temperature steam to scrub them thoroughly rather than scrubbing with detergent in cold or lukewarm water.
Comments (English): This is a truly honest review after using the LG dishwasher for about a year. Before I bought it, I was the most opposed to it, saying, "Scrubbing by hand is cleaner; why buy a dishwasher for just a few dishes?" But now that I have it in my home, I painfully understand why everyone calls the dryer, robot vacuum, and dishwasher the "three major home appliances." Here are some moments I was truly satisfied with: The satisfaction of seeing grease come off cleanly is incredible. Even if I put in a frying pan smothered in grease after grilling pork belly or bowls that held beef bone broth, they come out squeaky clean. It feels much cleaner and more hygienic to use high-temperature steam to scrub them thoroughly rather than scrubbing with detergent in cold or lukewarm water. You just run it at night and go to sleep (the door opens automatically). Once the wash is finished, the door slides open slightly, letting the steam escape. There is no risk of odors getting trapped, and it is incredibly convenient to have everything dry and fluffy by the next morning after just running it overnight. It gives me "free time" in the evenings. I used to sigh at the mountain of dishes piled up after cooking and eating, but now I just rinse the large food scraps with water, toss them into the dishwasher, and that's it. I can relax for at least 30 minutes after dinner. Here are some realistic downsides you must know before buying: It isn't completely "labor-free" (pre-washing is essential). It cannot perfectly remove hardened dried-on rice grains or burnt bottoms of pots. You still need to put in the effort to soak them in water beforehand or give them a quick pre-rinse. You also need some "dish Tetris" know-how. Since many Korean dishes are deep rice and soup bowls, you need a bit of skill (?) to stack them upright so the water flow is aligned properly. You will have to use your head a bit for the first few days trying to fit the dishes in. Definitely go for the large capacity. If you buy a 6-person or small model just because you are a 1-2 person household, you won't even be able to fit pots or pans, and you will end up washing them by hand. If space allows, I strongly recommend buying a 12-person capacity or larger. One-line summary: For those who struggle with family members over dishwashing turns or simply don't want to lift a finger after work, this is a sure-fire appliance that dramatically improves your quality of life and is definitely worth the money!

Sentence (English): There is no risk of odors getting trapped, and it is incredibly convenient to have everything dry and fluffy by the next morning after just running it overnight.
Comments (English): This is a truly honest review after using the LG dishwasher for about a year. Before I bought it, I was the most opposed to it, saying, "Scrubbing by hand is cleaner; why buy a dishwasher for just a few dishes?" But now that I have it in my home, I painfully understand why everyone calls the dryer, robot vacuum, and dishwasher the "three major home appliances." Here are some moments I was truly satisfied with: The satisfaction of seeing grease come off cleanly is incredible. Even if I put in a frying pan smothered in grease after grilling pork belly or bowls that held beef bone broth, they come out squeaky clean. It feels much cleaner and more hygienic to use high-temperature steam to scrub them thoroughly rather than scrubbing with detergent in cold or lukewarm water. You just run it at night and go to sleep (the door opens automatically). Once the wash is finished, the door slides open slightly, letting the steam escape. There is no risk of odors getting trapped, and it is incredibly convenient to have everything dry and fluffy by the next morning after just running it overnight. It gives me "free time" in the evenings. I used to sigh at the mountain of dishes piled up after cooking and eating, but now I just rinse the large food scraps with water, toss them into the dishwasher, and that's it. I can relax for at least 30 minutes after dinner. Here are some realistic downsides you must know before buying: It isn't completely "labor-free" (pre-washing is essential). It cannot perfectly remove hardened dried-on rice grains or burnt bottoms of pots. You still need to put in the effort to soak them in water beforehand or give them a quick pre-rinse. You also need some "dish Tetris" know-how. Since many Korean dishes are deep rice and soup bowls, you need a bit of skill (?) to stack them upright so the water flow is aligned properly. You will have to use your head a bit for the first few days trying to fit the dishes in. Definitely go for the large capacity. If you buy a 6-person or small model just because you are a 1-2 person household, you won't even be able to fit pots or pans, and you will end up washing them by hand. If space allows, I strongly recommend buying a 12-person capacity or larger. One-line summary: For those who struggle with family members over dishwashing turns or simply don't want to lift a finger after work, this is a sure-fire appliance that dramatically improves your quality of life and is definitely worth the money!

'그릇 테트리스' 노하우가 필요해요우리나라 그릇은 오목한 밥그릇, 국그릇이 많다 보니 물살이 잘 맞도록 세워 넣는 기술(?)이 좀 필요합니다. 처음 며칠은 그릇 끼워 넣느라 머리 좀 쓰셔야 해요. 용량은 무조건 큰 걸로 가세요1~2인 가구라고 6인용이나 작은 거 사시면 냄비나 프라이팬은 넣지도 못하고 결국 손설거지하게 됩니다. 자리만 된다면 무조건 12인용 이상으로 사시는 걸 강력 추천합니다. 한 줄 요약설거지 때문에 가족끼리 순번 정하며 눈치 싸움하거나, 퇴근 후 손가락 하나 꼼짝하기 싫은 분들에겐 삶의 질을 수직 상승시켜 주는 돈값 확실한 가전입니다!

Sentence (English): I used to sigh at the mountain of dishes piled up after cooking and eating, but now I just rinse the large food scraps with water, toss them into the dishwasher, and that's it.
Comments (English): This is a truly honest review after using the LG dishwasher for about a year. Before I bought it, I was the most opposed to it, saying, "Scrubbing by hand is cleaner; why buy a dishwasher for just a few dishes?" But now that I have it in my home, I painfully understand why everyone calls the dryer, robot vacuum, and dishwasher the "three major home appliances." Here are some moments I was truly satisfied with: The satisfaction of seeing grease come off cleanly is incredible. Even if I put in a frying pan smothered in grease after grilling pork belly or bowls that held beef bone broth, they come out squeaky clean. It feels much cleaner and more hygienic to use high-temperature steam to scrub them thoroughly rather than scrubbing with detergent in cold or lukewarm water. You just run it at night and go to sleep (the door opens automatically). Once the wash is finished, the door slides open slightly, letting the steam escape. There is no risk of odors getting trapped, and it is incredibly convenient to have everything dry and fluffy by the next morning after just running it overnight. It gives me "free time" in the evenings. I used to sigh at the mountain of dishes piled up after cooking and eating, but now I just rinse the large food scraps with water, toss them into the dishwasher, and that's it. I can relax for at least 30 minutes after dinner. Here are some realistic downsides you must know before buying: It isn't completely "labor-free" (pre-washing is essential). It cannot perfectly remove hardened dried-on rice grains or burnt bottoms of pots. You still need to put in the effort to soak them in water beforehand or give them a quick pre-rinse. You also need some "dish Tetris" know-how. Since many Korean dishes are deep rice and soup bowls, you need a bit of skill (?) to stack them upright so the water flow is aligned properly. You will have to use your head a bit for the first few days trying to fit the dishes in. Definitely go for the large capacity. If you buy a 6-person or small model just because you are a 1-2 person household, you won't even be able to fit pots or pans, and you will end up washing them by hand. If space allows, I strongly recommend buying a 12-person capacity or larger. One-line summary: For those who struggle with family members over dishwashing turns or simply don't want to lift a finger after work, this is a sure-fire appliance that dramatically improves your quality of life and is definitely worth the money!

'그릇 테트리스' 노하우가 필요해요우리나라 그릇은 오목한 밥그릇, 국그릇이 많다 보니 물살이 잘 맞도록 세워 넣는 기술(?)이 좀 필요합니다. 처음 며칠은 그릇 끼워 넣느라 머리 좀 쓰셔야 해요. 용량은 무조건 큰 걸로 가세요1~2인 가구라고 6인용이나 작은 거 사시면 냄비나 프라이팬은 넣지도 못하고 결국 손설거지하게 됩니다. 자리만 된다면 무조건 12인용 이상으로 사시는 걸 강력 추천합니다. 한 줄 요약설거지 때문에 가족끼리 순번 정하며 눈치 싸움하거나, 퇴근 후 손가락 하나 꼼짝하기 싫은 분들에겐 삶의 질을 수직 상승시켜 주는 돈값 확실한 가전입니다!

Sentence (English): It cannot perfectly remove hardened dried-on rice grains or burnt bottoms of pots.
Comments (English): This is a truly honest review after using the LG dishwasher for about a year. Before I bought it, I was the most opposed to it, saying, "Scrubbing by hand is cleaner; why buy a dishwasher for just a few dishes?" But now that I have it in my home, I painfully understand why everyone calls the dryer, robot vacuum, and dishwasher the "three major home appliances." Here are some moments I was truly satisfied with: The satisfaction of seeing grease come off cleanly is incredible. Even if I put in a frying pan smothered in grease after grilling pork belly or bowls that held beef bone broth, they come out squeaky clean. It feels much cleaner and more hygienic to use high-temperature steam to scrub them thoroughly rather than scrubbing with detergent in cold or lukewarm water. You just run it at night and go to sleep (the door opens automatically). Once the wash is finished, the door slides open slightly, letting the steam escape. There is no risk of odors getting trapped, and it is incredibly convenient to have everything dry and fluffy by the next morning after just running it overnight. It gives me "free time" in the evenings. I used to sigh at the mountain of dishes piled up after cooking and eating, but now I just rinse the large food scraps with water, toss them into the dishwasher, and that's it. I can relax for at least 30 minutes after dinner. Here are some realistic downsides you must know before buying: It isn't completely "labor-free" (pre-washing is essential). It cannot perfectly remove hardened dried-on rice grains or burnt bottoms of pots. You still need to put in the effort to soak them in water beforehand or give them a quick pre-rinse. You also need some "dish Tetris" know-how. Since many Korean dishes are deep rice and soup bowls, you need a bit of skill (?) to stack them upright so the water flow is aligned properly. You will have to use your head a bit for the first few days trying to fit the dishes in. Definitely go for the large capacity. If you buy a 6-person or small model just because you are a 1-2 person household, you won't even be able to fit pots or pans, and you will end up washing them by hand. If space allows, I strongly recommend buying a 12-person capacity or larger. One-line summary: For those who struggle with family members over dishwashing turns or simply don't want to lift a finger after work, this is a sure-fire appliance that dramatically improves your quality of life and is definitely worth the money!

Comments (English): This is a truly honest review after using the LG dishwasher for about a year. Before I bought it, I was the most opposed to it, saying, "Scrubbing by hand is cleaner; why buy a dishwasher for just a few dishes?" But now that I have it in my home, I painfully understand why everyone calls the dryer, robot vacuum, and dishwasher the "three major home appliances." Here are some moments I was truly satisfied with: The satisfaction of seeing grease come off cleanly is incredible. Even if I put in a frying pan smothered in grease after grilling pork belly or bowls that held beef bone broth, they come out squeaky clean. It feels much cleaner and more hygienic to use high-temperature steam to scrub them thoroughly rather than scrubbing with detergent in cold or lukewarm water. You just run it at night and go to sleep (the door opens automatically). Once the wash is finished, the door slides open slightly, letting the steam escape. There is no risk of odors getting trapped, and it is incredibly convenient to have everything dry and fluffy by the next morning after just running it overnight. It gives me "free time" in the evenings. I used to sigh at the mountain of dishes piled up after cooking and eating, but now I just rinse the large food scraps with water, toss them into the dishwasher, and that's it. I can relax for at least 30 minutes after dinner. Here are some realistic downsides you must know before buying: It isn't completely "labor-free" (pre-washing is essential). It cannot perfectly remove hardened dried-on rice grains or burnt bottoms of pots. You still need to put in the effort to soak them in water beforehand or give them a quick pre-rinse. You also need some "dish Tetris" know-how. Since many Korean dishes are deep rice and soup bowls, you need a bit of skill (?) to stack them upright so the water flow is aligned properly. You will have to use your head a bit for the first few days trying to fit the dishes in. Definitely go for the large capacity. If you buy a 6-person or small model just because you are a 1-2 person household, you won't even be able to fit pots or pans, and you will end up washing them by hand. If space allows, I strongly recommend buying a 12-person capacity or larger. One-line summary: For those who struggle with family members over dishwashing turns or simply don't want to lift a finger after work, this is a sure-fire appliance that dramatically improves your quality of life and is definitely worth the money!

'그릇 테트리스' 노하우가 필요해요우리나라 그릇은 오목한 밥그릇, 국그릇이 많다 보니 물살이 잘 맞도록 세워 넣는 기술(?)이 좀 필요합니다. 처음 며칠은 그릇 끼워 넣느라 머리 좀 쓰셔야 해요. 용량은 무조건 큰 걸로 가세요1~2인 가구라고 6인용이나 작은 거 사시면 냄비나 프라이팬은 넣지도 못하고 결국 손설거지하게 됩니다. 자리만 된다면 무조건 12인용 이상으로 사시는 걸 강력 추천합니다. 한 줄 요약설거지 때문에 가족끼리 순번 정하며 눈치 싸움하거나, 퇴근 후 손가락 하나 꼼짝하기 싫은 분들에겐 삶의 질을 수직 상승시켜 주는 돈값 확실한 가전입니다!

Sentence (English): Definitely go for the large capacity.
Comments (English): This is a truly honest review after using the LG dishwasher for about a year. Before I bought it, I was the most opposed to it, saying, "Scrubbing by hand is cleaner; why buy a dishwasher for just a few dishes?" But now that I have it in my home, I painfully understand why everyone calls the dryer, robot vacuum, and dishwasher the "three major home appliances." Here are some moments I was truly satisfied with: The satisfaction of seeing grease come off cleanly is incredible. Even if I put in a frying pan smothered in grease after grilling pork belly or bowls that held beef bone broth, they come out squeaky clean. It feels much cleaner and more hygienic to use high-temperature steam to scrub them thoroughly rather than scrubbing with detergent in cold or lukewarm water. You just run it at night and go to sleep (the door opens automatically). Once the wash is finished, the door slides open slightly, letting the steam escape. There is no risk of odors getting trapped, and it is incredibly convenient to have everything dry and fluffy by the next morning after just running it overnight. It gives me "free time" in the evenings. I used to sigh at the mountain of dishes piled up after cooking and eating, but now I just rinse the large food scraps with water, toss them into the dishwasher, and that's it. I can relax for at least 30 minutes after dinner. Here are some realistic downsides you must know before buying: It isn't completely "labor-free" (pre-washing is essential). It cannot perfectly remove hardened dried-on rice grains or burnt bottoms of pots. You still need to put in the effort to soak them in water beforehand or give them a quick pre-rinse. You also need some "dish Tetris" know-how. Since many Korean dishes are deep rice and soup bowls, you need a bit of skill (?) to stack them upright so the water flow is aligned properly. You will have to use your head a bit for the first few days trying to fit the dishes in. Definitely go for the large capacity. If you buy a 6-person or small model just because you are a 1-2 person household, you won't even be able to fit pots or pans, and you will end up washing them by hand. If space allows, I strongly recommend buying a 12-person capacity or larger. One-line summary: For those who struggle with family members over dishwashing turns or simply don't want to lift a finger after work, this is a sure-fire appliance that dramatically improves your quality of life and is definitely worth the money!

Sentence (English): If space allows, I strongly recommend buying a 12-person capacity or larger.
Comments (English): This is a truly honest review after using the LG dishwasher for about a year. Before I bought it, I was the most opposed to it, saying, "Scrubbing by hand is cleaner; why buy a dishwasher for just a few dishes?" But now that I have it in my home, I painfully understand why everyone calls the dryer, robot vacuum, and dishwasher the "three major home appliances." Here are some moments I was truly satisfied with: The satisfaction of seeing grease come off cleanly is incredible. Even if I put in a frying pan smothered in grease after grilling pork belly or bowls that held beef bone broth, they come out squeaky clean. It feels much cleaner and more hygienic to use high-temperature steam to scrub them thoroughly rather than scrubbing with detergent in cold or lukewarm water. You just run it at night and go to sleep (the door opens automatically). Once the wash is finished, the door slides open slightly, letting the steam escape. There is no risk of odors getting trapped, and it is incredibly convenient to have everything dry and fluffy by the next morning after just running it overnight. It gives me "free time" in the evenings. I used to sigh at the mountain of dishes piled up after cooking and eating, but now I just rinse the large food scraps with water, toss them into the dishwasher, and that's it. I can relax for at least 30 minutes after dinner. Here are some realistic downsides you must know before buying: It isn't completely "labor-free" (pre-washing is essential). It cannot perfectly remove hardened dried-on rice grains or burnt bottoms of pots. You still need to put in the effort to soak them in water beforehand or give them a quick pre-rinse. You also need some "dish Tetris" know-how. Since many Korean dishes are deep rice and soup bowls, you need a bit of skill (?) to stack them upright so the water flow is aligned properly. You will have to use your head a bit for the first few days trying to fit the dishes in. Definitely go for the large capacity. If you buy a 6-person or small model just because you are a 1-2 person household, you won't even be able to fit pots or pans, and you will end up washing them by hand. If space allows, I strongly recommend buying a 12-person capacity or larger. One-line summary: For those who struggle with family members over dishwashing turns or simply don't want to lift a finger after work, this is a sure-fire appliance that dramatically improves your quality of life and is definitely worth the money!

Comments (English): #SamsungElectronicsEventParticipation. First of all, I was very worried about the refurbishment issue before purchasing the dishwasher. Putting aside the price or performance, my biggest concern was the refurbishment, but I am satisfied because they did a neat and excellent job. 1. Premium Seamless Design Unique to the Infinite Line. Handleless & Luxurious Satin Glass: The seamless design, which falls smoothly without handles, is combined with luxurious satin white glass material to create a clean "Kitchen Fit" that harmoniously fits into kitchen cabinets. Floor Display: Even without opening the front door during operation, the remaining time and progress status are projected onto the floor surface with soft lighting, allowing for intuitive and aesthetic monitoring. 2. Clean Water and Dedicated Cup Care: Built-in Water Purification Filter: By purifying the wash water itself to wash dishes, it minimizes water stains and ensures hygienic cleaning. With a spacious 3-tier shelf structure for 14-place settings, it can comfortably accommodate everything from large pots to large quantities of dishes. In particular, a dedicated bottom cup-specific wash zone is provided to stably clean cups, tumblers, and glasses, making it useful for washing delicate beverage containers. 3. Powerful Cleaning & Smart AI Features. 100° High-Temperature Steam Soaking: Even stubborn burnt-on rice or heavily greased dishes are thoroughly soaked with 100° high-temperature steam before rinsing, significantly reducing the burden of pre-washing. 4. Automatic Door Opening: After washing and drying are complete, the door opens automatically to naturally release internal moisture, preventing odors and ensuring a perfectly dry finish. We are a family of five, and since our children are growing, we have frequent snacks. Sentence (English): I was SO excited to get my new dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Should've Read Reviews First ] || ---------------- || I was SO excited to get my new dishwasher. It replaced a 28 year old model that wasn't worth fixing anymore. Now? I called in the warranty by the 5th day after installation. GE's first available technician was 10-days out! They let me pay out of pocket to bring in my own guys so I still need to file for a refund. The technician said the drying element was working despite all the water dripping from the dishes in the top rack. He says I overloaded it and there wasn't enough space left for the drying element to work. Um, compared to my old dishwasher it was about 2/3 of a normal load and both racks had empty areas. It was then that I finally read online reviews that GE dishwashers don't do a very good job of drying plastics and right as I was reading the review about frequent sprayer arm failures my technician was telling me I should send it back to GE for that very reason. He told me they fail after 1-2 years of normal use. Great! Its not very clear how to attach photos and videos of how the last load was loaded and the amount of water that cascaded off the top rack when I pulled it out it. If they are attached, you be the judge. For my part, it's a buyer beware product. If I could send it back, I would in a heartbeat.

Comments (English): [ This one is very nice, but miss my old Bosch ] || ---------------- || We installed a new Bosch diswasher 23 years ago when we bought our house and I remodeled the kitchen. best appliance I've ever owned. It never needed a repair until four weeks ago when the circulation pump stopped working. I called the repair shop and he explained that Bosch doesn't make parts for that dishwasher anymore and there are no aftermarket parts available either. He said the only options are try and find a used pump or buy a new Bosch and enjoy another 23 trouble free years. I asked him if I should consider another brand and he said Bosch is the best so I opted for the the best. That being said the install was not as easy as it could have been as Bosch decided to change from a hard wired electric hook up to a plug in and moved the electric and water hook up to the rear instead of the front and designed very little room outside the rear of the unit to accomodate a receptical box in the cabinet. When the dishwasher was delivered the installer said he could not install it as the electrical needed a box and outlet and he could not do that. Since there was not enough room between the back of the unit and the back wall for an electrical box, I had to have a receptacle box and outlet installed in the sink cabinet. Also the drain hose was different and had to buy an adapter to fit the garbage disposal dw drain nipple where as my older bosch fit perfect. The next troublesome part was screwing the mounting tabs into the underside of the countertop. Bosch changed to location from the outer edge on each side of the unit to approx 6 inches in on each side. I had no wood strips at the new locations to screw into. So more labor and material to measure, cut and install a wood mounting strip in order to secure the new unit. The new unit is louder than old one even though the specs shows it is supposed to be quieter. not enough to worry about though. I've only been able to run 1 cycle so far and the dishes all came out dripping wet. I called Bosch and he said to go online and download the instruction manual and follow the instructions to set up the machine. I'm hopefull this will be an excellent trouble free dishwasher, but I will say I'm disappointed in Bosch for changing the exterior cabinet dimensions and the hook ups. it made for added frustration after the sale.

Sentence (English): The dishwashing functions are highly effective, with particularly strong drying at end of cycle.
Comments (English): [ Good function, some flaws to interior ] || ---------------- || The dishwashing functions are highly effective, with particularly strong drying at end of cycle. The new touch controls are very nice, and it's So quiet that the light letting you know that it's operating is almost a necessity, not just a convenience. However, the interior racks are not well-designed. The third rack, for tableware, is a easy to dump things into, but requires handling everything individually to put things away, and it restricts the use of the center rack for wine glasses or tall water glasses. You can remove it, and we have. The basket provided as an alternative is on the small side and must be placed on the right-hand side of the bottom rack. It has square corners, so it cannot be placed at the very front of the rack for easy accessibility when just loading tableware. It does not rest on the base of the rack, but must be hooked over the side of the rack. I have seen other Bosch dishwashers with this configuration where one of the hooks has broken off. The tines on the racks seem designed for specific functions rather than variable uses, and part of the bottom rack on the right is left blank, presumably to allow the tableware basket to be put anywhere along that side. The door on our previous dishwasher ( a Miele) was very well balanced and would open easily and stay open at any degree. This one really has to be pushed almost all the way open to stay at all, which makes opening it a little to pop a single item either into a rack or the basket unnecessarily tricky. We'll get used to it, but it's not ideal. Rack design should be maximally flexible, and the dish basket should fit on either side all the way to the front.

Sentence (English): After a two-week journey following the order, I finally managed to get it installed with difficulty.
Comments (English): After a two-week journey following the order, I finally managed to get it installed with difficulty. The sink height didn't match, so I had to cut the marble countertop. I was also frustrated during the installation process because I saw various instances of shoddy workmanship on the sink. I would like to thank the installer once again for taking such meticulous care of everything. I ordered this because of my back pain, and I am satisfied as it definitely reduces the time I spend standing at the sink. At first, I wondered if pre-washing was necessary, but I can really feel the reduction in dishwashing labor just by doing the pre-washing. Although I rarely run the dishwasher because there are fewer than five dishes a day from morning to evening on weekdays, making me wonder if it was too inefficient or unsuitable for my household, the difference between washing dishes and not washing them is significant. Oh, another downside is that I only have coated pans and woks. I heard that putting them in shortens the lifespan of the coating, so I was debating whether or not to replace the appliance just for the dishwasher; for now, I plan to not use it and replace it gradually. It is also a bit difficult to distinguish what can and cannot be put in. I mainly use it on weekends, and as a two-person household, I hardly use it on weekdays, but since the outer dimensions are the same for all dishwashers, I chose the 14-place setting model. The bigger, the better! Also, I just found this out, but you have to leave the door slightly ajar. Apparently, if you don't leave it open quite like in the photo reviews, odors can seep into the dishwasher. I didn't know that. They say you should leave a small vent open, even if not quite to that extent. Just so you know.
Comments (Original): 주문후 2주간의 여정 후 어렵게 설치했습니다.싱크대 높이가 안맞아 대리석 잘라냈어요. 설치과정중 싱크대에 여러가지 날림 시공이 보여서 열받기도 했구요. 설치기사님이 여러모로 세심하게 챙겨주셔서 다시 한 번 감사드리네요.저는 허리아파서 주문했는데 확실히 싱크대에 서있는 시간이 줄어들어서 만족합니다. 처음엔 애벌해야하는데 괜찮나 싶었는데..애벌만해도 설거지하는 노동력이 줄어든게 체감이 됩니다. 비록 평일은 하루에 아침부터 저녁까지 식기가 5개이하밖에 안나와서 돌리지 못해서 식세기 사용이 너무 비효율적인가 우리 가정엔 안맞나 싶었지만 설거지를 하고 안하고의 차이는 크더라구요. 아 또 단점인게 냄비나 궁중팬이 코팅팬 밖에 없어서 이걸 넣으면 코팅수명이 준다길래 식세기때문에 바꿔야하나 말아야하나 고민하다 우선은 사용은 안하고 천천히 바꿔가려구요. 넣을 수 있는 것 없는 것이 구별하기가 좀 어려운 점이 있네요.주로 주말사용에 2인가구고 평일엔 거의 사용하진 않지만 어차피 식세기 외경사이즈는 같아서 14인용 선택했습니다.거거익선!그리고 저는 처음 안 사실인데 문을 어느정도 살짝 열어놔야하더라구요. 안그러면 냄새가 식세기안에 스며들 수 있데요. 저는 몰랐네요 ㅎㅎ  사진리뷰처럼 저정도까진 아니더러도 조금 숨구멍정도는 열어둬야한데요. 참고하세요

Sentence (English): I checked my utility bill records, and it was 40,000-50,000 won from summer through November (I think it was just the bottle washer and formula dispenser up until then).
Comments (English): I checked my utility bill records, and it was 40,000-50,000 won from summer through November (I think it was just the bottle washer and formula dispenser up until then). Suddenly, it jumped to 70,000 won in December, 100,000 won in January, and 80,000 won in February. Realizing something was off, I stopped using the dishwasher, and it went back to the 50,000 won range starting in March. Since it was the middle of winter, I did turn on the heated humidifier as well! For reference, it seems like around 50,000 won is the baseline for our household. Now that I'm graduating from the bottle washer and the cooling dispenser, I'm hoping the bill will drop a little. I'm finally planning to try using the dishwasher again. Since the door opens automatically as long as you place the dishes so the water drips, natural drying seems fine too.

Sentence (English): We bought this Kitchenaid dishwasher to replace a dishwasher that was only 3 years old.
Comments (English): [ Piece of Junk ] || ---------------- || We bought this Kitchenaid dishwasher to replace a dishwasher that was only 3 years old. Being highly annoyed that our old dishwasher only lasted 3 years, we decided to spend a little more money and invest in a machine with higher consumer ratings and reviews. We bought this directly from the company and paid for installation and haul away of our old dishwasher. The installers installed it with the bottom panel on backwards and not correctly lined up, so we had to fix it after we discovered it when they left. They also tested it with the warranty info card still in the dishwasher, so we had to piece it back together, soaking wet. I shrugged it off and was just excited for the new machine. We ran a load two days later and everything was fine. Four days after that we ran it again only to have it start beeping an hour into the cycle. Perplexed, I had to Google what was going on. The clean button was flashing 10 times and then 4 times. Everything I googled said it was something to do with a diverter leak. I immediately panicked and pulled the bottom panel off to make sure there were no leaks or water. Thankfully there wasn't. I canceled the cycled and had it drain and then tried to run it again on an express cycle. The same thing happened. It was a full load of dishes on three racks, so I had to manually wash a gazillion dishes by hand while I put in a request for service. Oh, and all this happened while my husband was traveling for work for the week and I had my two kids by myself. A technician came out two days later and said it needed a new sump/pump. What? This is a BRAND NEW machine? It was a week old and only ran once! How does this even happen? So not only did we have to deal with no dishwasher for 8 days after the old one broke and we got the new one, but now we have to wait another week for the part to be ordered and come in. I absolutely hate having workers in the house and have had to deal with people messing my floors up and cleaning after them two times now, and will be three after the part comes in. The delivery people left black marks all over my kitchen floor and counters. I'm so annoyed and frustrated! Kitchenaid was supposed to be a quality brand! Forget it. I'll never buy anything from them again and advise others not to either. Why are you producing machines that have broken parts? This is INSANE! I wish I could return the whole thing and get my money back. This is NOT the brand for a busy family who expects quality products. It's only made my life more stressful, not less.

Sentence (English): #SamsungElectronicsEventParticipation.
Comments (English): #SamsungElectronicsEventParticipation. I was debating what to buy using this Samsung event opportunity, and I ended up ordering a dishwasher. Honestly, since we're a dual-income couple and only eat one or two meals a day at most, I hesitated a lot, wondering if it was just a luxury. There was also a lot of talk about pre-washing, so I even considered not buying it. To start with the conclusion, I am extremely satisfied. I completely understand why it's ranked among the top three dishes. Just the fact that I no longer have to spend time on washing dishes has made things so much easier. I used to be someone who hated letting dishes pile up, so I would wash them immediately. But now, just rinsing them roughly with water, gathering them, and running them through the dishwasher all at once is a whole new world. It fits in more space than I expected, so I think it would be fine to gather them up and wash them all at once. They come out so fluffy and dry that I wonder if it really washes that thoroughly. It's great that even heavy dishes are handled all at once. I just wash them quickly, stack them neatly, go to sleep, and then tidy up in the morning. The surroundings don't get messy, and organizing is easy. I used to spend a lot of time washing even the few dishes I had after meals, but now that I can just run it, relax, and go to sleep, the burden of washing dishes is gone. I use the Frosh Green Lemon Mini, and there is absolutely no smell. There is no water stain, and everything is so fluffy. I still lack the stacking technique, so I definitely need to study that. But even when I stack them haphazardly, it’s so easy that I wonder, "How does this even work?" The performance is great, and the design is so pretty. It’s bigger than I expected, but it doesn't look messy and fits in well. The installer was so kind and explained everything about how to use it. They even asked for my opinion to fit it into my lifestyle. They also secured the hoses neatly and perfectly. I uploaded a picture of the hole size for reference, as that is just right. They installed it quickly and explained everything kindly, so I was able to use it for the first time with a good feeling. I had it installed facing forward because of the stand above the sink. When I was searching online, I thought I absolutely had to place it near the sink. But actually, I like it; it hides the unsightly back view. The dishwasher is installed looking nice, and it’s not inconvenient at all to put the dishes right next to it after washing them. I am extremely satisfied; this is a must-have. Sentence (English): This is my third LG dishwasher.
Comments (English): This is my third LG dishwasher. I have been using models with progressively larger sizes, starting with the 6-place, then 12-place, and finally 14-place models. I purchased this product because it allows me to use it without cutting the wooden cover under the sink. Compared to the 12-place model (purchased in 2020), the advantages include a compartment for easily placing tablet detergent in the dish basket and a separate compartment for kitchen knives. However, the disadvantage lies in the dish basket; the adjustable plate size function is significantly less than before, making it very inconvenient when loading medium to large plates. I think I will continue to use it with satisfaction every day, and if you are considering buying a dishwasher, I would confidently recommend this one. '와~ 완전 신세계!'라는 말이 절로 나왔습니다. 손으로 설거지할 때보다 훨씬 깔끔하게 세척되고, 컵이나 그릇도 물자국 없이 반짝반짝해서 괜히 문을 열어보고 또 열어보게 되더라고요. 특히 기름기 있는 프라이팬이나 냄비도 깨끗하게 세척돼서 너무 만족스러웠습니다.무엇보다 설거지하는 시간이 아까웠는데 이제는 식기만 넣고 버튼 하나 누르면 끝이라 그 시간에 다른 집안일을 하거나 쉬면서 여유를 가질 수 있다는 점이 가장 큰 장점인 것 같아요. 하루에도 몇 번씩 '진작 살 걸!'이라는 생각을 합니다. 새 아파트 입주하면서 가장 잘한 선택 중 하나라고 자신 있게 말할 수 있습니다.디자인도 고급스럽고 네이처 베이지 색상이 주방과 자연스럽게 잘 어울려 인테리어까지 한층 더 예뻐졌어요. 소음도 생각보다 조용해서 사용 중인지 신경 쓰이지 않았고, 세척 후에는 그릇이 뽀득뽀득 깨끗하게 나와 기분까지 좋아집니다.이제는 설거지가 스트레스가 아니라 버튼 한 번으로 끝나는 일이 되었네요. 매 끼니 먹고 나서도 부담이 없고, 가족들과 보내는 시간도 더 늘어난 것 같습니다. 앞으로도 매일매일 만족하며 사용할 것 같고, 식기세척기 고민하시는 분들이 계시다면 정말 자신 있게 추천드리고 싶습니다. 저처럼 사용 첫날부터 '신세계다!'라는 말을 하시게 될 거예요.

The plate is sparkling! ] || ---------------- || The appliance I was looking forward to the most when moving into my new apartment was the dishwasher, and after using it myself, I immediately understood why so many people call it an essential appliance. '와~ 완전 신세계!'라는 말이 절로 나왔습니다. 손으로 설거지할 때보다 훨씬 깔끔하게 세척되고, 컵이나 그릇도 물자국 없이 반짝반짝해서 괜히 문을 열어보고 또 열어보게 되더라고요. 특히 기름기 있는 프라이팬이나 냄비도 깨끗하게 세척돼서 너무 만족스러웠습니다.무엇보다 설거지하는 시간이 아까웠는데 이제는 식기만 넣고 버튼 하나 누르면 끝이라 그 시간에 다른 집안일을 하거나 쉬면서 여유를 가질 수 있다는 점이 가장 큰 장점인 것 같아요. 하루에도 몇 번씩 '진작 살 걸!'이라는 생각을 합니다. 새 아파트 입주하면서 가장 잘한 선택 중 하나라고 자신 있게 말할 수 있습니다.디자인도 고급스럽고 네이처 베이지 색상이 주방과 자연스럽게 잘 어울려 인테리어까지 한층 더 예뻐졌어요. 소음도 생각보다 조용해서 사용 중인지 신경 쓰이지 않았고, 세척 후에는 그릇이 뽀득뽀득 깨끗하게 나와 기분까지 좋아집니다.이제는 설거지가 스트레스가 아니라 버튼 한 번으로 끝나는 일이 되었네요. 매 끼니 먹고 나서도 부담이 없고, 가족들과 보내는 시간도 더 늘어난 것 같습니다. 앞으로도 매일매일 만족하며 사용할 것 같고, 식기세척기 고민하시는 분들이 계시다면 정말 자신 있게 추천드리고 싶습니다. 저처럼 사용 첫날부터 '신세계다!'라는 말을 하시게 될 거예요.

Sentence (English): A quiet, all-steel-tub dishwasher for well under $1k!
Comments (English): [ Such a find: ] || ---------------- || A quiet, all-steel-tub dishwasher for well under $1k! Plus, Bosch's reputation (fingers crossed) for reliability. I have had a Bosch dishwasher for several years and love it. It is super quiet and warned me when there was a leak, which I was able to fix myself (which points to another plus: available, quality parts). When I needed a second dishwasher for an in-law unit, I expected the best of Bosch to be too costly, but I was wrong: Bosch making a durable, basic (100 Series) dishwasher further boosts its reputation. This more basic unit does not have the 3rd rack that my other one does, but the rack layout is still highly functional. It also is not as quiet, but is much quieter (soft white noise) than the one I replaced. My only nitpick is leveling: It took way too long. Bosch should provide a plastic tool that fits in the front feet to turn them more easily. Better yet: Bosch should change the shape of the front leveling feet so that they can be easily turned with a flat screwdriver.

Comments (English): #SamsungElectronicsEventParticipation. Escape the dishwashing hell! My quality of life has changed thanks to AI Custom Wash and Hot Air Drying. My old appliances were getting old, and my wrists were hurting so much from hand-washing my family's dishes and pots every time. After much consideration, I replaced them with the Samsung BESPOKE AI 14-Place (DW80F73X1UEWS) built-in model. The result is so satisfying that I seriously wish I had bought it sooner! 1. Clean built-in design & ample storage for 14 places. The Essential White color fits perfectly with the kitchen base cabinets without any gaps, so it looks clean and doesn't detract from the interior at all. Being a 14-place model, the interior space is really spacious. The top, middle, and bottom shelf configuration is efficient and height-adjustable, so large pots, frying pans, and even tall tumblers all fit in at once. It gives me peace of mind knowing I can gather all the dishes from dinner and run them all at once. 2. Smart AI Custom Wash+ & Powerful cleaning performance. The AI Custom Wash+ feature, which automatically sets the course based on the amount of dishes and soiling level, is incredibly convenient. I used to worry about having to scrub hard for pre-washing due to grease stains on grilled pans or burnt-on rice in bowls, but thanks to the steam soaking function and the 4-stage 3D water jets, dishes come out spotlessly clean without any extra scrubbing. 3. 100° Hot Air Drying + Automatic Door Opening. When buying a dishwasher, the most important factor for me was 'drying,' and since this product features 100° hot air drying and an automatic door opening after the wash, the level of freshness is truly different. Aside from water pooling in the backs of concave dishes, even glass cups and plastic tableware dry completely without any water stains, allowing them to be put away in the cupboard immediately. 4. Low Noise & SmartThings Integration. Even if I run it late at night in the Night Low Noise mode while I sleep, there is almost no noise or vibration, so I don't have to worry about it. Being able to check the wash completion time and progress immediately via SmartThings app notifications is also incredibly useful. For those considering a dishwasher, I highly recommend the combination of the 14-place setting large capacity and hot air drying!

Clean built-in design & ample storage for 14 places. The Essential White color fits perfectly with the kitchen base cabinets without any gaps, so it looks clean and doesn't detract from the interior at all.
